title.narrative: DRC Corruption Landscape Evaluation and Assessment of Risks. Unveiling vulnerabilities in regulatory framework and practices that enable corruption.

description.narrative:
In the DRC, the tax relied system, originally designed as a legitimate instrument of tax and justice, suffers from flawed implementation characterized by regulatory instability, a lack of procedural safeguards, and excessive discretionary power granted to tax officials.
The International Development Law Organization (IDLO) seeks to collaborate with relevant government institutions, especially the Ministry of Justice, to foster a stable and enabling environment for private sector development, trade, and investment in the DRC by reducing corruption risks of tax reassessment to contribute to this long-term goal. The project aims to undertake a Corruption Risk Assessment (CRA) to identify risks associated with the Congolese tax reassessment policies.
In parallel, the Netherlands has expressed a strong commitment to a transparent and attractive economic environment in the DRC. Through various diplomatic initiatives, notably exchanges between the Ambassador of the Netherlands and the Congolese authorities, the Kingdom of Netherlands (as lead of Inter-donor group on the business environment in DRC) affirmed its willingness to support structural reforms aimed at improving economic governance, to strengthen accountability and reduce corruption in the tax field. This convergence of interests between the DRC and its international partners reflects a common desire to consolidate the fiscal framework and stimulate sustainable investments based on increased regulatory predictability.
The result of this activity will be a validated CRA Report reflecting broad stakeholder input, ensuring institutional buy-in, and laying the foundation for follow-up actions and policy reforms. The validated report will also serve as a reference tool for continued dialogue and coordination among national authorities, oversight bodies, and international partners in strengthening integrity within tax administration, as well as for the development of the roadmap.
